servers.name: Gigwa MCP
servers.attribution: Anestis Gkanogiannis and contributors
servers.installation: Install gigwa-mcp separately into a Python >=3.10 environment; configure GIGWA_URL and optional paired GIGWA_USER/GIGWA_PASS.
servers.effects: Tools may upload data, modify Gigwa, or write local result files; inspect each tool before invocation.

servers.name: Chorus
servers.attribution: Dmitry Penzar, Lorenzo Ruggeri, Rosalba Giugno, Luca Pinello and contributors
servers.installation: Install the pinellolab/chorus source project and provision its oracle environments, model weights and references separately. The PyPI package named chorus is unrelated. Set executable_path to the installed chorus-mcp.
servers.effects: Predictions can consume GPU/CPU, write reports, and download missing model assets inside the upstream server. Pre-provision assets when offline.

servers.name: MaveDB-Link
servers.attribution: Bernt Popp and mavedb-link contributors
servers.installation: For stdio, install the source project's dependencies in Python >=3.12 and set workdir to that checkout and executable_path to its Python. The author-documented HTTP service is available with transport='http'.
servers.effects: Reads local MaveDB mirrors or contacts the MaveDB API; HTTP mode sends tool arguments to the author's hosted service.

servers.name: BioMCP
servers.attribution: Ian Maurer, GenomOncology and contributors
servers.installation: Install genomoncology/biomcp separately; its PyPI distribution is biomcp-cli, not the unrelated biomcp distribution. The installed executable is biomcp.
servers.effects: Contacts upstream biomedical APIs according to the selected tool; some sources require credentials.

servers.name: Juicebox MCP
servers.attribution: Jim Robinson, Douglass Turner and contributors
servers.installation: Prepare the official source checkout and npm dependencies separately, then set workdir to the checkout and executable_path to Node if necessary.
servers.effects: Starts the MCP server and local browser communication service; visualization tools may require an attached Juicebox frontend and network datasets.

servers.name: GeneChat MCP
servers.attribution: Nate Costello and GeneChat contributors
servers.installation: Install and initialize GeneChat and its local genome/annotation databases separately. GENECHAT_CONFIG optionally selects an existing TOML configuration.
servers.effects: Reads configured local genomes; returned tool results can include individual genotypes.

servers.name: GenePattern MCP
servers.attribution: GenePattern team and contributors; underlying platform: Reich et al., GenePattern 2.0 (2006)
servers.installation: Install the official source checkout requirements separately with Python >=3.11. Set workdir to the checkout, executable_path to that Python, and GENEPATTERN_KEY to an existing API token.
servers.effects: Selected tools can submit GenePattern jobs, upload data, or download files. Uses GenePattern cloud by default or the explicitly configured GENEPATTERN_URL.

servers.name: BrAPI MCP
servers.attribution: Casey Hand (cyanheads) and contributors; community BrAPI implementation
servers.installation: Separately prepare the pinned @cyanheads/brapi-mcp-server release/source with its dist build and dependencies; set workdir to the package root and executable_path to Node >=24. The bridge never runs npm, npx, bunx or an installer.
servers.effects: Queries BrAPI servers; opt-in upstream tools can submit observations or export local data. Connection aliases and dataframes require call_mcp_workflow to preserve a session.
limitations: Interface integration does not implement genomic selection or validate breeding predictions.

servers.name: Ensembl MCP (cyanheads)
servers.attribution: Casey Hand (cyanheads) and contributors; community wrapper, not an Ensembl-authored server
servers.installation: Separately prepare the pinned @cyanheads/ensembl-mcp-server build and dependencies; set workdir to the package root and executable_path to Node >=24.
servers.effects: Sends selected gene, sequence, variant and homology queries to Ensembl REST or the configured mirror.

servers.name: BioThings MCP
servers.attribution: Anton Kulaga and Longevity Genie contributors
servers.installation: Install the pinned longevity-genie/biothings-mcp project separately in Python >=3.10; use its installed biothings-mcp entry point.
servers.effects: Queries BioThings services and may write cached/exported result data under the upstream output directory.

servers.name: gget MCP
servers.attribution: Anton Kulaga, Newton Winter and Longevity Genie contributors; gget method authors retain their own credit
servers.installation: Install gget-mcp and its separately specified gget dependencies in Python >=3.10; the verified command is gget-mcp stdio.
servers.effects: Queries gget-supported services; selected tools may run external searches, load models, download assets or write outputs.
limitations: Individual tools and their dependencies require separate validation; tool count is not an independent-algorithm count.

servers.name: UCSC Genome MCP
servers.attribution: Henry Lydecker (hlydecker) and contributors; community UCSC wrapper
servers.installation: Prepare the pinned source checkout and its requirements in Python >=3.10, set workdir to the checkout and executable_path to that Python. Use the existing hyphenated ucsc-genome-mcp.py script; upstream README/packaging also mention nonexistent underscore filenames.
servers.effects: Sends genome, track, region and sequence queries to UCSC and caller-selected public assembly hubs.
limitations: The pinned upstream script sometimes encodes application errors as ordinary text. DNAKit recognizes its verified error prefixes and preserves the original flag as upstream_isError when normalizing them. Other tool-specific content still needs inspection.

servers.name: Open Targets MCP
servers.attribution: Nick Ren and contributors; community Open Targets wrapper
servers.installation: Install nickzren/opentargets-mcp separately in Python >=3.10; set executable_path to its interpreter. Uses the verified Python module entry point with explicit stdio.
servers.effects: Queries Open Targets evidence; results are research evidence and do not establish treatment suitability.

servers.name: Plant Genomics MCP
servers.attribution: Jaret Arnold (musharna) and contributors; community integration
servers.installation: Install the pinned plant-genomics-mcp Python distribution and dependencies separately. The plant-genomics-mcp entry point selects stdio; no HTTP token is needed for this local transport.
servers.effects: Queries plant genomics services and may submit selected sequences to NCBI BLAST. Configure the named NCBI contact-email variable before BLAST use.
limitations: The advertised hosted Tailscale endpoint has a bearer-token gate; it is not configured as an anonymous DNAKit endpoint.

servers.name: BioContextAI Knowledgebase MCP
servers.attribution: Malte Kuehl and the BioContextAI authors/contributors listed in the upstream citation
servers.installation: Install biocontext_kb separately in Python >=3.12. DNAKit fixes MCP_ENVIRONMENT=DEVELOPMENT for the verified stdio entry point.
servers.effects: Queries the selected biomedical knowledge services. The public hosted endpoint is described by its authors as testing-only and subject to fair use.
limitations: Data-source licenses and access limitations are separate; Google Scholar and KEGG are local-only in the upstream project.

servers.name: GrEBI
servers.attribution: EMBL-EBI SPOT / EBISPOT GrEBI contributors
servers.installation: Select transport='http' for the author-documented development service. Local deployment is a separate Java/API plus graph-database and HPC data-pipeline task; no local startup recipe is claimed here.
servers.effects: Sends queries to the EMBL-EBI development knowledge-graph service.
limitations: Development endpoint, without a production availability guarantee; no graph database or pipeline has been deployed by DNAKit.

servers.name: EBI Tools MCP (QuentinCody)
servers.license: Not specified in repository snapshot; remote service only, no upstream code bundled
servers.attribution: QuentinCody and repository contributors; community implementation, not an EMBL-EBI release
servers.installation: Select transport='http' for the repository author's published Cloudflare Worker MCP service. No standalone Node stdio entry point is present; no mcp-remote/npx helper is required by DNAKit.
servers.effects: Selected tools can submit sequences to EMBL-EBI Job Dispatcher and retrieve job results through a community-hosted service.
limitations: No LICENSE/LICENCE file or package license declaration was verified. Hosted transport availability is separate from job/scientific validation.

servers.name: GWAS MCP (muslus)
servers.attribution: ZaEyAsa (upstream package/LICENSE attribution) and muslus repository contributors
servers.installation: Prepare the pinned muslus/gwas-mcp source and its dependencies in an isolated Python >=3.10 environment, then point executable_path at that interpreter. Avoid assuming that the separately published gwas-mcp distribution has identical code.
servers.effects: Queries genomic evidence services; selected QC/association tools may execute local analyses and write files.
limitations: Repository owner and package author differ; the exact pinned source is the verified implementation. Individual analysis results have not been validated by DNAKit.

servers.name: NCBI Database MCP (hpend2373)
servers.license: MIT declared in pyproject.toml; standalone license text not found
servers.attribution: hpend2373 and Bio-MCP Project contributors (pyproject attribution)
servers.installation: Prepare the pinned NCBI-Database-MCP checkout and its requirements, set workdir to the checkout and executable_path to its Python. Uses the README-supported standard MCP script rather than executing its shell installer/launcher.
servers.effects: Queries NCBI gene/sequence/GEO resources; selected results can contain supplied gene or region queries.
limitations: MIT is a project metadata declaration; no standalone LICENSE file was found at the pinned revision.

servers.name: PubMed MCP (cyanheads)
servers.attribution: Casey Hand (cyanheads) and contributors; community literature server
servers.installation: Prepare the pinned @cyanheads/pubmed-mcp-server build and dependencies separately, then set workdir to the package root and executable_path to Node >=24.
servers.effects: Sends biomedical literature queries to PubMed/PMC, Europe PMC and optional Unpaywall; document permissions remain with the original sources.
limitations: Literature infrastructure, not a DNA prediction algorithm.

servers.name: ENCODE Toolkit
servers.attribution: Dr. Alex M. Mawla and contributors
servers.installation: Install the Python encode-toolkit distribution separately and set executable_path to its interpreter. DNAKit invokes the verified Python module directly; it does not use the npm shim which can bootstrap uv/Python.
servers.effects: Queries ENCODE experiments and files; selected upstream tools may download data, create workflows or manage local credential state.
limitations: Zenodo records are software archives, not automatically peer-reviewed papers. This bridge does not redistribute ENCODE Toolkit code.

servers.name: ToolUniverse
servers.attribution: Shanghua Gao, Marinka Zitnik and ToolUniverse paper/project contributors
servers.installation: Install the pinned ToolUniverse distribution and required provider dependencies separately. Use the installed tooluniverse console script; unlike the README uvx --refresh example, this bridge does not refresh or install anything.
servers.effects: Starts the compact ToolUniverse MCP catalog. Selected tools may contact services, load models, execute programs or write files according to their provider definitions.
limitations: Cross-disciplinary aggregate: not every exposed tool is DNA-related, and tool counts are not independent-algorithm counts. Provider credentials/dependencies must be configured separately.

servers.license: Remote provider terms; the marketplace does not grant an independent server-code license

servers.installation: Select transport=http. The provider-published endpoint supports anonymous MCP initialization and tools/list as verified on 2026-09-20. No local installer is run.
capabilities: article metadata, full text and copyright status
servers.effects: Queries are sent to the named public biological/literature service. Returned articles and data retain provider-specific terms.
limitations: Only initialization and tools/list were exercised; provider query results and scientific conclusions were not validated.

servers.license: Remote provider terms; the marketplace does not grant an independent server-code license

servers.installation: Select transport=http. The provider-published endpoint supports anonymous MCP initialization and tools/list as verified on 2026-09-20. No local installer is run.
capabilities: live Open Targets GraphQL schema and queries
servers.effects: Queries are sent to the named public biological/literature service. Returned articles and data retain provider-specific terms.
limitations: Only initialization and tools/list were exercised; provider query results and scientific conclusions were not validated.

servers.name: 10x Genomics Cloud MCP
servers.license: MIT (MCP connector); separate 10x Cloud and TXG CLI terms apply
servers.attribution: 10x Genomics, Inc.
servers.installation: Separately prepare and unpack the upstream 10x Genomics MCP bundle, including its server/, node_modules/ and platform bin/ files. Set workdir to that unpacked bundle, executable_path to installed Node.js >=18, and the named TXG_CLI_ACCESS_TOKEN environment variable. DNAKit does not download a bundle or TXG binary.
capabilities: Cell Ranger and ATAC analysis submission and monitoring
servers.effects: Selected tools can upload sequencing files, read or modify cloud projects and references, and start paid analyses. Upstream only sets accept-payment=true when that tool argument is explicitly supplied.
limitations: Source and manifest entry points are verified. No 10x account, access token, TXG binary, cloud job or scientific result was exercised. This is one component of the Anthropic marketplace entry.

servers.name: Seqeron Sequence MCP
servers.attribution: Gabor Barat (copyright holder per LICENSE) and Seqeron contributors
servers.installation: Source-based: clone the pinned commit, install the .NET 10 SDK (net10.0 target), set workdir to the checkout root and executable_path to the dotnet executable; the first dotnet run builds the project. No environment variables are read. This entry covers only the Seqeron.Mcp.Sequence server; the repository ships ten more servers (Parsers, Alignment, Analysis, Annotation, MolTools, Population, ...) that are not cataloged.
servers.effects: Pure local computation on sequences passed as tool arguments; the Sequence server's code makes no network calls and reads or writes no files.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: not started here: needs the .NET 10 SDK; tool names were checked against the source.

servers.name: SmartAPI MCP (BioThings core)
servers.attribution: BioThings Team and smartapi-mcp contributors
servers.installation: pip install smartapi-mcp (PyPI, version 0.6.0 at verification) into a Python >=3.10 environment; the catalog arguments select the core BioThings API set with the generic five-tool facade forced on (MyGene.info, MyVariant.info, MyChem.info, MyDisease.info, MyGeneSet.info, MyTaxon.info). No credentials are needed; optionally set SMARTAPI_LOG_LEVEL or LOG_LEVEL.
servers.effects: Fetches API specs from the SmartAPI registry (smart-api.info) at startup and sends query and lookup requests (GET /query, GET and POST by id) to the public BioThings services; no files are written and no credentials are sent. The cataloged --api_set biothings_core selects only BioThings APIs.
limitations: Facade mode (--facade on) is forced because the default auto threshold (10 BioThings APIs) would instead emit hundreds of per-API tools for this 6-API set; non-standard endpoints of individual APIs are not reachable in non-strict facade mode.
In an environment with a SOCKS proxy configured, install 'socksio' (httpx[socks]) or the server exits at start.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 5 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: just-prs MCP
servers.attribution: Anton Kulaga, Newton Winter and just-prs-mcp contributors
servers.installation: pip install just-prs-mcp (PyPI, version 0.5.0 at verification) into a Python >=3.13 environment (the optional 'reference' extra adds pgenlib on non-Windows); default mode is essentials and no API key is needed. Optionally set PRS_MCP_MODE (essentials or extended), PRS_MCP_CACHE_DIR, PRS_MCP_DEFAULT_GENOME_BUILD, PRS_MCP_DEFAULT_PANEL, PRS_MCP_DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT.
servers.effects: Queries the PGS Catalog and downloads scoring files, reference data and sample genomes (Zenodo) into a local cache, reads local VCF or array files, writes normalized Parquet files, job state, logs and trait HTML reports to the cache directory; extended mode adds bulk downloads and a HuggingFace upload tool that needs an HF token, which this entry deliberately does not expose.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 20 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: DNALLM MCP Server
servers.attribution: Zhangtaolab and DNALLM contributors
servers.installation: Install the PyPI package dnallm (Python >=3.11, installs the dnallm-mcp-server console script), plus a torch build suited to the hardware; because the wheel does not ship dnallm/mcp/configs, also keep a source checkout and set workdir to it so the default --config dnallm/mcp/configs/mcp_server_config.yaml resolves.
servers.effects: Loads the DNA language models named in the YAML configuration (downloading weights from Hugging Face or ModelScope on first use), runs local CPU/GPU inference, writes temporary VCF files for variant scoring, and may save predictions under the output_dir set in the model inference configs; no sequence data is sent to a DNALLM-operated service.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: not started here: needs a torch build and model files; tool names were checked against the source.

servers.name: just-dna-agents MCP
servers.attribution: DNA-Seq and just-dna-agents contributors (Anton Kulaga)
servers.installation: Install the just-dna-agents-mcp and just-dna-agents packages from the pinned GitHub repository subdirectories (neither name resolves on PyPI although the README says the package is published) into a Python >=3.14 environment; optional JUST_DNA_AGENTS_MCP_OUTPUT_DIR and JUST_DNA_AGENTS_MCP_RESOLVE_WITH_ENSEMBL settings control compilation.
servers.effects: validate_spec reads a caller-given spec directory; compile_module writes parquet files to the output directory (default current directory) and, with Ensembl resolution enabled, may use an Ensembl variation reference whose parquet cache the repository's resolver downloads from the Hugging Face dataset just-dna-seq/ensembl_variations; the compiler internals live in the separate just-dna-compiler package and were not inspected.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: not started here: needs Python >=3.14; tool names were checked against the source.

servers.name: Genomi
servers.attribution: Exon Research and Genomi contributors
servers.installation: Install the exon-research/genomi source project (not on PyPI; Python >=3.10, depends on a git-pinned gxl-paperclip) so that the genomi console script exists, then run genomi install to materialize reference libraries; optionally set GENOMI_HOME to relocate its data directory (default ~/.genomi).
servers.effects: Parses user-supplied genome files into a local Active Genome Index and evidence database under GENOMI_HOME, keeps a local journal, runs background jobs, and genomi.install downloads public reference libraries; returned results can contain individual genotypes, and optional lab operations may contact external evidence providers.
limitations: Hand-written JSON-RPC 2024-11-05 server (not FastMCP); the default tools/list exposes only the base operations, and capability operations such as variant.resolve are reached through genomi.invoke after reading the matching skill document.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 37 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: Galaxy MCP
servers.attribution: Dannon Baker, the Galaxy Project and Galaxy MCP contributors
servers.installation: Install the PyPI package galaxy-mcp (Python >=3.10; PyPI has 1.11.2 while the pinned commit is 1.12.0.dev0) and set GALAXY_URL and GALAXY_API_KEY for the target Galaxy instance.
servers.effects: Connects to the configured Galaxy server with the API key and can run tools and workflows, create histories, pages and user-defined tools, and upload local files or URLs (stdio mode reads and writes local paths), so it modifies the remote Galaxy account and submits data to that server.
limitations: General-purpose bioinformatics platform bridge: no tool is specific to DNA or genes; relevance comes from the Galaxy tools and workflows available on the configured instance.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 48 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: gnomAD MCP
servers.attribution: Masaru Koido and gnomad-mcp contributors
servers.installation: Clone the pinned koido/gnomad-mcp checkout (not on PyPI, no console script) and install its dependencies (fastmcp, gql, aiohttp, httpx) in Python >=3.13; set workdir to the checkout and executable_path to that Python. No environment variables or credentials are needed.
servers.effects: Sends GraphQL queries over HTTPS to the public gnomAD browser API at https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/api (gene, variant, region and metadata lookups); the server tools do not write local files or modify remote data.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 12 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: Addgene MCP
servers.attribution: Anton Kulaga and Longevity Genie contributors
servers.installation: pip install addgene-mcp==0.1.3 (PyPI, Python >=3.12) or install the pinned repository separately; the installed console script is addgene-mcp and 'addgene-mcp stdio' starts the stdio server. No credentials are required; MCP_HOST, MCP_PORT and MCP_TRANSPORT only affect the HTTP/SSE modes.
servers.effects: Scrapes https://www.addgene.org through a Scrapy subprocess for plasmid search and sequence information (Scrapy may keep a local HTTP cache); download_sequence fetches a GenBank or SnapGene file from Addgene and writes it to the current working directory or a caller-chosen directory, creating it if needed.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 4 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: AlphaGenome MCP (JoLab)
servers.attribution: Taeho Jo and alphagenome-mcp contributors
servers.installation: Install with npm install -g @jolab/alphagenome-mcp (Node.js >=18, installed executable alphagenome-mcp) plus pip install 'alphagenome>=0.9.0' numpy in a Python >=3.10 interpreter; set ALPHAGENOME_API_KEY (and optionally ALPHAGENOME_PYTHON to that interpreter, ALPHAGENOME_TIMEOUT_MS).
servers.effects: Sends variant coordinates and alleles through a Python subprocess to the Google DeepMind AlphaGenome API (Atlas lookups or live inference) using the caller's API key; no local files are written by the tools. The upstream README states the API is free for non-commercial use only, so commercial use is restricted and requires accepting DeepMind's AlphaGenome Terms of Use and rate limits.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: not started here: needs Node.js >=18 (16 installed) and an AlphaGenome API key; tool names were checked against the source.

servers.name: Locus
servers.attribution: Matthew McNulty and Locus contributors
servers.installation: Install separately into a Python >=3.11 environment from the pinned source (pip install git+https://github.com/mattsmcnulty/locus.git@24b046548e9e976fc7e28395b86ff262e6d3c343; not the unrelated PyPI package named locus), then build the local DuckDB genome store with the upstream pipeline (locus download all; locus pipeline); set LOCUS_DATA_DIR (or LOCUS_DB_PATH) to the data directory because the default location is derived from the source tree.
servers.effects: Most tools run read-only queries against the local DuckDB store; ask_about and variants_in_study send rsIDs to the Ensembl REST API and write temporary marker files under the Locus work directory, variants_in_study queries the GWAS Catalog, and literature_for sends the query to NCBI PubMed E-utilities.
limitations: Requires a prebuilt Locus DuckDB store from the user's own VCFs; tools return an error note until it exists.
Upstream documents macOS Apple Silicon only; AlphaMissense data it downloads is CC-BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) although the code is MIT.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 22 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: MCP Sequence Simulation
servers.attribution: Corey Hudson and mcp-sequence-simulation contributors
servers.installation: Install separately from the pinned source checkout with npm install && npm run build (Node.js with npm; package.json declares no engines field), then set workdir to the checkout and keep dist/server.js; no environment variables are used.
servers.effects: Pure local computation that returns simulated sequences, trees and FASTQ text in the tool response; the source contains no network calls, file writes or environment access.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: not started here: needs Node.js >=18 (16 installed) and a build; tool names were checked against the source.

servers.name: NCBI SRA MCP Server
servers.attribution: ncbi-sra-mcp-server contributors (CSI Genomics and Data Analytics Core)
servers.installation: Not on PyPI: install separately from the pinned source checkout in a Python >=3.11 environment (pip install -r requirements.txt, which provides fastmcp), set workdir to the checkout and executable_path to that Python; optionally set NCBI_EMAIL and NCBI_API_KEY, and install sra-tools (prefetch, fasterq-dump) for toolkit downloads.
servers.effects: Queries NCBI Entrez E-utilities and the ENA portal API; sra_download starts background jobs that create the destination directory (default ./downloads) and write .sra or FASTQ files via urllib or the sra-tools prefetch/fasterq-dump subprocesses.
limitations: Launched through 'python -c' because running sra_mcp_server.py as __main__ prints a plain-text banner to stdout before mcp.run(); a stdio client that does not skip non-JSON lines would fail on it. Both forms were started with the FastMCP client and listed the six tools.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 6 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: bioinformatics-mcp
servers.attribution: Raony Guimaraes and bioinformatics-mcp contributors
servers.installation: Install separately into a Python >=3.11 environment from the pinned source (pip install "bioinformatics-mcp[full] @ git+https://github.com/raonyguimaraes/bioinformatics-mcp.git@b607d569a95fad247125894efa4b3e14e024c5e2"; the README's PyPI name returned 404 on PyPI); no environment variables are used.
servers.effects: Database tools send queries to NCBI E-utilities, UniProt, Ensembl and STRING over HTTPS; save_anndata and export_obs_table write files to caller-supplied paths; other tools read local sequence, VCF, BAM, CSV and AnnData files and hold datasets in memory.
limitations: Single-cell, spatial and variant tools need optional extras; the full tool set is 72 tools, many for single-cell RNA-seq rather than DNA.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 70 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: Rewire Genomics MCP
servers.attribution: Tim Richardson and rewire-bio/genomics-mcp contributors
servers.installation: Install the pinned repository checkout into a Python >=3.12,<3.13 environment (pip install of the checkout, with --no-binary pybigwig; needs a C compiler plus libcurl and zlib development files for remote bigWig/bigBed); the upstream docs say there is no PyPI package although PyPI lists rewire-genomics-mcp 0.1.0 by the same author, so prefer the checkout. Optionally set GENOMICS_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS to the folders the server may read, and EGA credentials only for controlled EGA data.
capabilities: bounded genomic region reads (BAM, VCF, FASTA, bigWig)
servers.effects: Calls public services (EGA, ENA, ENCODE, GEO, NCBI, Ensembl, HGNC, ClinVar, gnomAD, UniProt, Open Targets) over HTTPS and reads local files under the allowed roots; fetch_file, cancel_transfer and convert_sra_run write downloaded files into the server work directory (default under the XDG cache), values from private files go to external APIs only when a call sets allow_external_annotation.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 24 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: Bioinformatics MCP Server (NCBI and UniProt)
servers.attribution: AiAgentKarl
servers.installation: pip install bioinformatics-mcp-server (PyPI 0.1.0) into a Python >=3.11 environment; no environment variables or API keys are needed. The wheel installs a top-level package named src, so use a dedicated environment. Pin the dependency 'mcp<2': the upstream package leaves mcp unpinned and its server fails to import under mcp 2.x (FastMCP was renamed).
capabilities: NCBI nucleotide and protein sequence retrieval
servers.effects: Read-only HTTPS queries to NCBI E-utilities (Gene, ClinVar, Taxonomy, Nucleotide, PubMed) and the UniProt REST API; every request sends tool and a fixed contact email parameter to NCBI, nothing is written locally.
limitations: Tool error messages and instructions are partly in German.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 10 tools; every name in tool_names was present.

servers.name: UniProt MCP Server (smaniches)
servers.attribution: Santiago Maniches and TOPOLOGICA LLC
servers.installation: pip install uniprot-mcp-server (PyPI 1.3.9) into a Python >=3.11 environment; optionally set UNIPROT_PIN_RELEASE (for example 2026_01) to pin the UniProt release and UNIPROT_MCP_CACHE_DIR to enable the offline replay cache directory. No API key is needed.
servers.effects: Read-only HTTPS queries to rest.uniprot.org and www.uniprot.org, NCBI E-utilities (ClinVar) and the AlphaFold EBI service; ID mapping submits identifiers to UniProt as a job, and uniprot_replay_from_cache reads local files from UNIPROT_MCP_CACHE_DIR; live responses are not written to that cache in the pinned code.
limitations: Protein-centric (41 tools in total); only the variant, ClinVar, disease, ID-mapping and proteome tools touch gene-level data. tool_names lists a verified subset of the 41.
servers.startup_check: 2026-10-14: started over stdio in a clean environment and listed 41 tools; every name in tool_names was present.
